data.narrative:
Telesat Lightspeed is a public-stage space and aerospace company that has raised C$2.1B to date under CEO Dan Goldberg. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of four same-sector, same-stage peers: Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B), and Astroscale ($840M).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Across the four public Space & Aerospace comparables, the median valuation is $5.2B, with a wide range spanning $840M at the low end to $40.0B at the high end. This dispersion reflects material heterogeneity in the peer set—likely driven by differences in revenue scale, customer concentration, and path to profitability. A revenue-based multiple approach (P/S anchoring) cannot be applied due to the absence of disclosed revenue figures for the target. The Space & Aerospace public comp set shows a sector median P/S of 27.4x across six tickers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL), but without target revenue data, this method cannot be operationalized.

The triangulated valuation range is $4.4B to $6.0B, with a central estimate of $5.2B. This single-method derivation reflects meaningful uncertainty around where Telesat Lightspeed sits within the peer distribution. Key unknowns include the company's revenue trajectory, customer diversification, and capital efficiency relative to the comparable set. The wide peer valuation range ($840M–$40.0B) itself signals that stage and sector alone are insufficient anchors; additional operational metrics are required to narrow the band further.
